name: Nala Sinephro
label: Warp
lede: She plays a pedal harp through modular synths, sits outside jazz's rules without ignoring them, and made a 45-minute album of ten pieces all called "Continuum" that Pitchfork ranked fifth of 2024.

eras.title: A harp, a jaw, a detour through Boston
eras.text: Born in Brussels to a Belgian piano-teacher mother and a Martinican-Guadeloupean jazz-saxophonist father, Sinephro arrived at music sideways: biochemistry first, then a school with a jazz department, then a pedal harp.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · AllMusic: Nala Sinephro
years.h: Brussels, a forest, and the harp at 16
years.p: Sinephro grew up outside Brussels and switched from a biochemistry track to an arts high school with a jazz department, where she found the pedal harp.
years.xp:
Wikipedia, citing press profiles, says her mother was a classical piano teacher and her father a jazz saxophonist of Martinican and Guadeloupean descent. It also says she developed a jaw tumor as a teenager and that, after it was removed, she spent a stretch going to Brussels clubs for hardcore dance music.

AllMusic puts her taking up the pedal harp at 16, after learning folk songs on violin by ear. Her time is split in the bio between Belgium and Martinique, where family lives.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · Still Listening: Endlessness review
years.h: One year at Berklee, then out the door
years.p: She enrolled at Berklee College of Music in Boston but left after a year, deciding her job as a sound engineer taught her more than the classes.
years.xp: A second jazz college in London followed, and she dropped out of that one quickly too, according to Wikipedia. The engineering habit stuck: her albums credit her with production, engineering and mixing alongside the playing.

eras.title: Tottenham, Steam Down and a radio show
eras.text: In London she fell in with the jazz scene around Shabaka Hutchings and Nubya Garcia, played in a collective, and spent two years writing the music that became her debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · AllMusic: Nala Sinephro
years.h: Sinephro moves to Tottenham and joins [[Steam Down|1c8e9570-4f97-4452-bc3f-ac765757176b]]
years.p: She has lived in North London since 2018 and played with the Steam Down improvisation collective,, and worked with the [[London Contemporary Orchestra|47f3b634-a476-4ca7-930b-5ff9f46b133a]] scene.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the scene around Hutchings and Garcia helped her develop a sense of individuality in her style. AllMusic lists neo-soul singer [[Demae|5323e27d-ea62-4af4-883e-1c33a25f417a]] and LCO conductor [[Robert Ames|1174b084-89ec-47e1-9888-35301673f234]] among her early collaborators.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · AllMusic: Nala Sinephro
years.h: NTS gives her a monthly radio show
years.p: Her NTS program began in June 2020, a place to play the ambient and spiritual-jazz records she was steeped in.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · Beats Per Minute: Endlessness review
years.h: Lockdown in Martinique, tape recorder in hand
years.p: She spent months on the island where family lives and got into field recording, which fed the music that followed.

eras.title: Space 1.8
eras.text: A debut that arrived fully formed, on Warp, from sessions recorded years before anyone heard it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Space 1.8 · Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro · Warp: Space 1.8
years.h: Space 1.8: her debut, and her first release on Warp
years.p: Eight pieces for harp, modular synth and a rotating cast including [[Nubya Garcia|42dd1862-7255-47ed-8584-651abce3bf53]] and [[James Mollison|fa407068-5773-4dbe-a34a-6d1917d93fd4]], from tapes made in 2018 and 2019.
years.xp:
Sinephro wrote on piano, recorded pedal harp and modular synth parts at home, then took the material into Pink Bird studio with Garcia, Mollison, drummer Jake Long and bassists Twm Dylan and Wonky Logic, per Wikipedia. Warp lists it as catalog WARPCDD324.

Pitchfork gave it 8.3 and put it at No. 24 on its 50 best albums of 2021, according to Wikipedia. Metacritic scored it 85 from seven critics.

q: I reach a trance state. I'm almost sleepwalking.
years.src: The Afterword: Space 1.8 · Wikipedia: Nala Sinephro
years.h: The Guardian finds out how the harp gets played
years.p: In the paper's profile she described the trance state she works in, hands moving while she half sleeps.
years.xp: The Guardian profile, by Ammar Kalia, ran under that quote. She told the paper she has to surrender to the sound and might hold one note for ten minutes straight if that is what the moment calls for, a line also quoted in The Afterword's write-up. Pitchfork followed with its own profile in January 2022.

eras.title: Endlessness
eras.text: Five years after the tapes, a second album built as one continuous cycle, with a bigger band and a string ensemble.

years.h: Brooklyn church, one continuous suite, no breaks
years.p: Playing Endlessness live at St Ann & the Holy Trinity in Brooklyn Heights, her band ran the music as a single piece with modular synth, harp, drums and saxophone.
years.xp: A Black Noise reviewer wrote that the group played with so much restraint that they seemed to be holding space rather than filling it. There was no opener and no drinks, which made the room feel ceremonial.

years.p: Warp announced the album and shared its opener, a patient piece built on the arpeggio that runs through all ten tracks.

years.src: Album of the Year: Endlessness · Wikipedia: Endlessness · Still Listening: Endlessness review · Beats Per Minute: Endlessness review
years.p: Pitchfork's Daniel Felsenthal scored it 8.5 and it finished No. 5 on the site's best albums of 2024.
years.xp:
Sinephro played harp, keys and synths and produced it, with Rick David of Pink Bird as engineer. Players include Garcia and Mollison on saxophone, Morgan Simpson (ex-[[black midi|4afbef0a-05ee-4551-b0e0-f1f1870d8f1c]]) and Natcyet Wakili on drums, [[Sheila Maurice-Grey|2e358555-415c-478b-a0b5-b0b329170028]] on flugelhorn, [[Lyle Barton|cef6431a-9ea3-44f1-bfdc-9d16aae0ed39]] on keys, and Orchestrate's strings. A bass line from Alice Sinephro is sampled on Continuum 4.

Reviewers noted the synths are tuned to 432Hz. Felsenthal called it a "potent and intuitive second album" that imagines a music between ambient and jazz. Metacritic's aggregate was 83, per Wikipedia.

years.h: The year-end lists: Crack No. 3, BBC 6 Music, Uncut
years.p: Crack ranked Endlessness No. 3 of 2024 and The Line of Best Fit No. 6, with Paste at No. 10, plus lists from Bleep, Uncut, Exclaim! and Rough Trade.

eras.title: The Smashing Machine
eras.text: A director heard Endlessness and handed her a film.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smashing Machine · Resident Advisor: The Smashing Machine
years.h: Benny Safdie hires her to score The Smashing Machine
years.p: Safdie picked her after hearing Endlessness, for his A24 film about MMA fighter Mark Kerr, played by Dwayne Johnson. It was her first film score.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smashing Machine · Resident Advisor: The Smashing Machine
years.h: Eight tracks, 25 minutes, recorded at Abbey Road
years.p: Released on Warp and A24 Music the day the film opened, with Garcia, Mollison and Simpson back in the room; the vinyl followed on January 23, 2026.
years.xp: Reviews split. Pitchfork praised its "disarmingly rich, romantic sweep"; Rolling Stone found it "woozy" and at times soporific, and the Wall Street Journal called it jagged and discordant, per Wikipedia's summary.
play: The Smashing Machine (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
